title: The sl(2) weight system at c = -3/32 extends to a graph 4-invariant

journal_fit: The explicit graph invariant and its links with Lie algebra weight systems fit the journal's combinatorial and algebraic scope. The neighbouring c=3/8 specialization was treated in this journal.
contribution: The paper proves Conjecture 4.1 of Fomichev, Karev, Pavutnitskiy and Usanov: the sl(2) weight system at c=-3/32 extends to a graph four-invariant. The explicit signed-count construction works on every finite graph and agrees with the matrix-defined weight system on every chord diagram. This revision adds a normal-form proof and clarifies verification scope.

formalization_scope: The universal extension theorem and its matrix-trace definition are formalized in Lean 4.34.1 with pinned Mathlib. At the unchanged proof-source commit, the complete build and four endpoint axiom reports passed with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Python exact checks were rerun locally; Julia, C and C++ passed in the archived full run. The grouping proof for part (a) and the added faithful-action lemma are supplied in the written argument; no new formalization of the abstract Weyl algebra is claimed.
abstract_tex: We prove unconditionally the conjecture of Fomichev, Karev, Pavutnitskiy and Usanov that the specialization of the $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ weight system at $c=-3/32$ extends to a $4$-invariant of graphs. The extension is $\xi(G)=(-32)^{-n}S_G(-2)$, where $S_G(N)$ counts with signs the assignments of $2$-element subsets of $\{1,\dots,N\}$ to the $n$ vertices of $G$.
abstract_plain: We prove unconditionally the conjecture of Fomichev, Karev, Pavutnitskiy and Usanov that the specialization of the mathfraksl(2) weight system at c=-3/32 extends to a 4-invariant of graphs. The extension is xi(G)=(-32)^-nS_G(-2), where S_G(N) counts with signs the assignments of 2-element subsets of 1,dots,N to the n vertices of G.
